findings.title: Denial cache key omits identity type, so an anonymous denial is served to the renderer
findings.description:
`userPermDenialCacheKey` builds the key from namespace, raw `UserUID`, action, name and parent only. The denial lookup in `Check` (`pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116-121`) runs before any identity-type dispatch.

Anonymous and render identities both carry ID `"0"` (`pkg/services/user/identity.go:296-298`), and both reach this service as `anonymous:0` and `render:0` (`service_test.go:803`, `:853`). Their denial keys are therefore identical.

Failure sequence:
1. An anonymous viewer is denied `dashboards:read` on a dashboard, and the denial is cached for 30s.
2. The renderer checks the same dashboard and folder within that window.
3. The renderer gets `Allowed: false` from the denial cache, although `getRendererPermissions` would grant `*`.

The error fails closed, but it is a wrong authorization result. The regular permission cache avoids this by using a dedicated `anonymousPermCacheKey` and never caching the renderer.

Two related weaknesses sit in the same key:
- **Ambiguous delimiter:** fields are joined with `_`, which is legal in Grafana UIDs. `name="a_b", parent="c"` and `name="a", parent="b_c"` produce the same key, so one denial can be returned for a different resource.
- **Shared prefix:** the key reuses the `.perm_<uid>_<action>` prefix of `userPermCacheKey` in the same backing cache. A cross-read is only prevented by JSON unmarshal failing between `bool` and `map[string]bool`.

Fix: include the identity type, use a distinct prefix such as `.perm_denial_`, and use a delimiter that cannot appear in UIDs (or length-prefix or hash the fields).

findings.title: Denied checks now bypass the permission cache and hit the database per resource
findings.description:
The cache read was removed from `getUserPermissions` and `getAnonymousPermissions` (`service.go:379-380`, `:423-424`). `Check` now falls through to `getIdentityPermissions` whenever the cached permissions do not grant access.

A fresh cache entry that correctly says "no access" therefore triggers a full permission query for every distinct `(name, parent)`. Singleflight only collapses concurrent calls. A caller that checks N inaccessible resources one by one within 30s now causes N permission queries, where the base code caused one.

The denial cache only helps on a repeat of the exact same resource. It also adds one entry per `(user, action, name, parent)`; `name` and `folder` are not validated in `validateCheckRequest`, so the number of entries is request-controlled and unbounded.

Consider skipping the database fallback when the cached permission set was written very recently, or otherwise rate-limiting refreshes per user and action.

findings.title: Denial-cache test passes without the denial cache, and new paths are untested
findings.description:
"Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" says it seeds an allowing permission "to prove this is not checked". It actually seeds `{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}`. `checkPermission` tests the map value (`service.go:558`), so the cached permissions do not allow. The fallback then queries the empty `fakeStore` from `setupService` and denies anyway. The test stays green if the denial-cache lookup is deleted; the seeded value should be `true`.

Other gaps:
- No test asserts that a database-backed denial writes to `permDenialCache` (`service.go:153-155`).
- No test asserts that an allow does not write a denial entry.
- No test covers `getCachedIdentityPermissions` for anonymous or render identities, which is where the collision above would have been caught.
- `TestService_getUserPermissions` lost its only `cacheHit: true` case. The `cacheHit` field and its branches (`service_test.go:337`, `:367-369`, `:388-392`) are now dead code.

findings.title: Errors from the cached lookup are treated as cache misses, and metric meaning shifts
findings.description:
`getCachedIdentityPermissions` can return real errors, such as a failed `GetUserIdentifiers` store lookup or an unsupported identity type, not only `cache.ErrNotFound`. `Check` and `List` (`service.go:180-192`) treat any error as a miss and call `getIdentityPermissions`, which repeats the failing lookup before the error surfaces. Branching on `errors.Is(err, cache.ErrNotFound)` would avoid the duplicate call.

`permission_cache_usage` also changes meaning:
- Render requests always count as `cache_hit="false"`.
- Anonymous requests are now counted; previously they were not.
- A cache hit that does not grant access counts as a miss.

Dashboards built on this metric will shift.

findings.title: `NoopCache` is exported and undocumented, and client construction is duplicated
findings.description:
`NoopCache` is exported from `pkg/services/authz` but used only at `rbac.go:103`. It has no doc comment, and its receiver is named `lc`, apparently copied from a local-cache type. Unexporting it and adding a `var _ cache.Cache = (*NoopCache)(nil)` assertion would tighten it.

Removing `newRBACClient` leaves two near-identical `authzlib.NewClient(...)` blocks (`rbac.go:101-105`, `:160-167`). Keeping the helper with a cache parameter would avoid that.

Disabling the client-side cache for the in-process client looks intentional, since the server keeps its own cache. A one-line comment saying so would help.
